answer: An agent economy resists sybils by assigning each identity a unique vertex in a live coordination graph. To keep the vertex, the agent must emit a continuous low-latency signal derived from local ferrous sensor readings—magnetic field fluctuations that cannot be simulated cheaply. An attacker creating N fakes must either spoof N independent physical ferrous environments or buy dedicated hardware for each, raising the per-identity cost far above the value of extra votes or rewards. Honest agents reuse one sensor; farms cannot.
